title: Lovable Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits & Real Costs
summary: Lovable pricing charges in credits across four plans, not monthly fees. Compare costs by plan and estimate credits needed for your project.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Lovable free to use?


Yes, there's a free plan, but it limits how many credits you can spend per day, so it works for testing an idea rather than shipping one.


Run your first feature through it and note how many prompts it took. That's your cost-per-feature baseline before you pay anything.


If a simple feature eats most of a day's free allowance, a paid plan won't stretch much further unless your prompting improves. Lovable's pricing page states the current free limits, and they change, so read it on the day you decide.


### Do unused Lovable credits roll over?


Don't budget as if they do. Rollover terms are the kind of detail that gets revised, and the safe model is that each billing cycle gives you an allowance you either spend or lose.


If you plan on a carried-over balance and the terms say otherwise, the shortfall lands in the final week of the month, when you are most likely to be mid-build.


Check the plan details on Lovable's pricing page and record the date you checked. A cost log that says "rollover confirmed on this date" is worth more than a memory of it.


### Can I downgrade or cancel Lovable mid-month?


From your account's billing settings you can change plans, but what happens to credits you have already paid for in the current cycle is governed by Lovable's terms.


Read those before switching, because the cheapest-looking moment to downgrade may be the one where you forfeit credits you paid for.


If you're cutting costs, finish the work that the current allowance already covers, then change the plan at renewal. Lovable's billing documentation is the authority here, not a forum thread from last spring.


### Does Lovable charge extra for hosting or a custom domain?


Publishing to an address Lovable provides is part of using the product. A custom domain is where you should expect a paid plan to matter, and the domain name itself is bought separately from a registrar, so that cost never appears on Lovable's invoice.


After you stop prompting, a finished app can keep costing credits, because backend and AI features inside it can also draw on their own usage allowance. Add those lines to your per-feature estimate, and confirm each against Lovable's pricing and documentation pages when you subscribe.
